  MISS refused=False expected=True  "position('(' IN a) + (SELECT x FROM other)"  scrubbed -> 'position('
  MISS refused=False expected=True  'trim(a || (SELECT x FROM t)'  scrubbed -> 'trim('

2	
3	Every rule here exists because the engine accepts the violation without complaint. Two of
4	them accept it and then corrupt data quietly. Conventions section 1.4, ADR 0004.
5	"""
6	
7	from __future__ import annotations
8	
9	import re
10	from collections.abc import Sequence

12	from pathlib import Path
13	
14	import yaml

16	from adss.model import Model
17	from adss.names import Schema

19	# An attribute expression may read its own row: a column, a cast of one, a CASE over them, or
20	# arithmetic over them. Anything else is a join, and every join must come from a declared
21	# relationship. M5, and ADR 0007 for where the line between arithmetic and meaning is drawn.
22	_REACHING = re.compile(r"\b(select|join|from|over|group\s+by)\b", re.IGNORECASE)
23	_AGGREGATE = re.compile(r"\b(sum|count|min|max|avg|any_value|array_agg)\s*\(", re.IGNORECASE)
24	
25	# Standard SQL spells several same-row functions with FROM as part of their syntax, and their
26	# FROM introduces nothing. Matching it made the checker refuse `extract(DAY FROM b - a)` -- the
27	# natural idiom for the very thing M5 permits -- and tell the reader it reached beyond its row.
28	# A refusal whose stated reason is wrong sends someone looking for a problem that is not there.
29	_KEYWORD_FROM = re.compile(r"\b(extract|substring|trim|overlay|position)\s*\(", re.IGNORECASE)
30	
31	# A key expression is compared by shape, not by spelling: only the casting decides what
32	# VARCHAR the two sides of an edge produce. Everything not a type or an operator is a name.
33	_IDENTIFIER = re.compile(r"[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z_0-9]*")
34	_LITERAL = re.compile(r"'[^']*'")
35	_SHAPE_WORDS = frozenset(
36	    {

38	        "as",
39	        "concat",
40	        "coalesce",

42	        "char",
43	        "text",

54	        "real",
55	        "float",
56	        "date",
57	        "timestamp",
58	        "boolean",
59	        "uuid",
60	    }
61	)

63	ATTRIBUTE_KEYS = frozenset({"id", "transformation_expression"})
64	
65	REQUIRED_STRATEGY = "FULL_LOG"
66	REQUIRED_CLOCK = "extracted_at"

70	    """A mapping the engine would accept and should not."""

104	def read_mapping(path: Path) -> Mapping:
105	    document = yaml.safe_load(path.read_text())
106	    tables = [
107	        Table(
108	            table=str(table["table"]),
109	            primary_keys=tuple(table.get("primary_keys", [])),
110	            ingestion_strategy=str(table.get("ingestion_strategy", "")),
111	            effective_timestamp_expression=str(

113	            ),
114	            expressions=tuple(
115	                str(attribute["transformation_expression"])
116	                for attribute in table.get("attributes", [])
117	            ),
118	            declared=tuple(tuple(attribute) for attribute in table.get("attributes", [])),
119	        )
120	        for group in document["mapping_groups"]
121	        for table in group["tables"]
122	    ]
123	    relationships = [
124	        Relationship(
125	            id=str(declared["id"]),
126	            source_table=str(declared["source_table"]),
127	            target_expression=str(declared["target_transformation_expression"]),
128	        )
129	        for group in document["mapping_groups"]
130	        for declared in group.get("relationships", [])
131	    ]
132	    return Mapping(
133	        path=path,
134	        entity_id=str(document["entity_id"]),
135	        tables=tuple(tables),
136	        relationships=tuple(relationships),

140	def check_mapping(mapping: Mapping) -> None:
141	    """Refuse what M1-M5 and M7 refuse, naming the rule that refused it.
142	
143	    M6 is about relationships and lands with the first one. M2 is checked for cardinality
144	    here; its key-shape clause -- a concat without a separator collapses 'A1' + '23' and
145	    'A12' + '3' into one key -- is review-only until there is a composite key to check.
146	    """
147	    where = mapping.path.name
148	    for table in mapping.tables:
149	        if not table.table.startswith(f"{Schema.DAS_STAGED}."):
150	            raise MappingError(
151	                f"{where}: M1 -- a mapping reads a {Schema.DAS_STAGED} object and nothing "
152	                f"else, never {table.table!r}. Reading the raw layer skips the contract's "
153	                f"casts, and a join here is business logic in the wrong layer."
154	            )
155	        if len(table.primary_keys) != 1:
156	            raise MappingError(
157	                f"{where}: M2 -- exactly one primary key. {list(table.primary_keys)} is read "
158	                f"as that many alternate identifiers, not as a composite key, and that mode "
159	                f"cannot be undone once loaded."
160	            )
161	        if table.ingestion_strategy != REQUIRED_STRATEGY:
162	            raise MappingError(
163	                f"{where}: M3 -- {REQUIRED_STRATEGY}, not {table.ingestion_strategy!r}. "
164	                f"FULL against a source holding more than one row per key inserts a "
165	                f"duplicate on every run, forever, and every presentation view hides it."
166	            )
167	        if table.effective_timestamp_expression != REQUIRED_CLOCK:
168	            raise MappingError(
169	                f"{where}: M4 -- a version is dated by {REQUIRED_CLOCK}, not "
170	                f"{table.effective_timestamp_expression!r}. The effective time of a fact is "
171	                f"when the system observed it; anything else dates it by something that is "
172	                f"not about the fact."
173	            )
174	        for expression in table.expressions:
175	            if reaching(expression):
176	                raise MappingError(
177	                    f"{where}: M5 -- {expression!r} reaches beyond its row. An expression "
178	                    f"that does is a join, and every join comes from a declared relationship."
179	                )
180	        for keys in table.declared:
181	            # A YAML flow mapping treats the commas inside a function call as its own
182	            # separators, so `{id: X, transformation_expression: f('a', b, c)}` silently
183	            # becomes the expression `f('a'` plus keys named `b` and `c)`. There is no YAML
184	            # error and nothing downstream notices: the truncated expression still reads its
185	            # own row, so M5 accepts it, and the engine is the first thing to object -- to SQL
186	            # nobody wrote. The stray keys are the signature, and they are the only one.
187	            stray = [key for key in keys if key not in ATTRIBUTE_KEYS]
188	            if stray:
189	                raise MappingError(
190	                    f"{where}: an attribute declares {stray}, which is not a key an attribute "
191	                    f"has. Almost always this is YAML flow style splitting an expression on "
192	                    f"the commas inside a function call -- write that attribute in block "
193	                    f"style, or quote the expression."
194	                )
195	        if not table.expressions:
196	            raise MappingError(
197	                f"{where}: M7 -- every mapped table carries at least one attribute. The "
198	                f"engine refuses an entity with none, at deploy rather than at review."
199	            )

202	def reaching(expression: str) -> bool:
203	    """Whether an expression leaves the row it is written on. M5.
204	
205	    Arithmetic and same-row functions do not, however they are spelled; a subquery, a join, a
206	    window or an aggregate does.
207	    """
208	    return bool(
209	        _REACHING.search(_without_keyword_from(expression)) or _AGGREGATE.search(expression)
210	    )
211	
212	
213	def _without_keyword_from(expression: str) -> str:
214	    """The expression with the syntactic FROM of each such function blanked, and nothing else.
215	
216	    Only that one token, and only when it is genuinely inside the call. An earlier version
217	    discarded the whole argument list, which excused the very thing M5 exists to stop: a
218	    subquery hidden in `extract(DAY FROM (SELECT ...))` became invisible. Taking simply the
219	    next FROM instead was no better -- in `trim(a) FROM elsewhere` the next one is the reach.
220	
221	    So the scan finds the first FROM at the call's own bracket depth, and gives up at the
222	    bracket that closes the call. It steps over single-quoted text, because a bracket inside a
223	    string literal is not a bracket, and a scan that believed otherwise would run off the end
224	    and hand the checker half an expression to judge.
225	    """
226	    out = expression
227	    for call in _KEYWORD_FROM.finditer(expression):
228	        found = _syntactic_from(out, call.end())
229	        if found is not None:
230	            out = out[:found] + " " * 4 + out[found + 4 :]
231	    return out
232	
233	
234	def _syntactic_from(expression: str, opened: int) -> int | None:
235	    """Where the FROM belonging to a call that opened at `opened` starts, if it has one."""
236	    depth, index = 1, opened
237	    while index < len(expression):
238	        character = expression[index]
239	        if character == "'":
240	            closing = expression.find("'", index + 1)
241	            index = len(expression) if closing == -1 else closing + 1
242	            continue
243	        depth += (character == "(") - (character == ")")
244	        if depth == 0:
245	            return None
246	        if (
247	            depth == 1
248	            and expression[index : index + 4].lower() == "from"
249	            and not expression[index - 1 : index].isalnum()
250	            and not expression[index + 4 : index + 5].isalnum()
251	        ):
252	            return index
253	        index += 1
254	    return None
255	
256	
257	def key_shape(expression: str) -> str:
258	    """A key expression with its column names removed, which is what M6 compares.
259	
260	    M6 asks that a relationship's target expression mirror the target entity's own key
261	    expression. It is the *shape* that has to match, not the spelling: a foreign key column is
262	    routinely named differently from the primary key it points at. What must not differ is the
263	    casting, because that is what decides the VARCHAR the two sides produce -- a bare column on
264	    one side and a cast on the other join to nothing at all.
265	    """
266	    parts: list[str] = []
267	    last = 0
268	    for literal in _LITERAL.finditer(expression):
269	        # A separator inside a concat is part of the shape and survives verbatim: 'A1' + '23'
270	        # and 'A12' + '3' are one key without it.
271	        parts.append(_without_names(expression[last : literal.start()]))
272	        parts.append(literal.group(0))
273	        last = literal.end()
274	    parts.append(_without_names(expression[last:]))
275	    return " ".join("".join(parts).split())
276	
277	
278	def _without_names(fragment: str) -> str:
279	    def anonymous(word: re.Match[str]) -> str:
280	        found = word.group(0).lower()
281	        if found in _SHAPE_WORDS:
282	            return found
283	        # A name immediately followed by "(" is a function, and a function decides the value
284	        # as surely as a cast does: lpad(x, 5, '0') and x produce different keys, and
285	        # anonymising the name would make them the same shape.
286	        called = fragment[word.end() : word.end() + 1] == "("
287	        return found if called else "?"
288	
289	    return _IDENTIFIER.sub(anonymous, fragment)
290	
291	
292	def check_relationships(mappings: Sequence[Mapping], model: Model) -> None:
293	    """Refuse what M6 refuses. Every one of its failures is silent in the built warehouse.
294	
295	    A mis-spelled `source_table` is skipped by the engine without a word, a differently shaped
296	    target expression makes pairs that join to nothing, and an edge no mapping loads makes no
297	    pairs at all. All three show up as an inherited key that is null everywhere, which reads
298	    as data rather than as a defect. ADR 0006.
299	    """
300	    loaded: list[tuple[Mapping, Relationship]] = [
301	        (mapping, edge) for mapping in mappings for edge in mapping.relationships
302	    ]
303	    declared = {edge.id for _, edge in loaded}
304	    modelled = {edge.id: edge for edge in model.relationships}
305	
306	    for edge_id in modelled:
307	        if edge_id not in declared:
308	            raise MappingError(
309	                f"M6 -- {model.path.name} declares {edge_id} and no mapping loads it. The "
310	                f"engine builds no pair object at all, so every join along that edge returns "
311	                f"null, which reads as 'these rows have no target' rather than as a gap."
312	            )
313	
314	    for mapping, edge in loaded:
315	        edge_id = edge.id
316	        where = mapping.path.name
317	        if edge_id not in modelled:
318	            expected = [candidate.id for candidate in model.edges_from(mapping.entity_id)]
319	            raise MappingError(
320	                f"{where}: M6 -- {edge_id} is not an edge {model.path.name} declares. An id "
321	                f"is <SRC>_<NAME>_<TGT>, so {mapping.entity_id} can load {expected or 'none'}. "
322	                f"The engine would build this pair object from the mapping alone: it would "
323	                f"work, and be an edge nothing explains."
324	            )
325	        declared = modelled[edge_id]
326	        if mapping.entity_id != declared.source_entity_id:
327	            raise MappingError(
328	                f"{where}: M6 -- {edge_id} runs from {declared.source_entity_id}, and this "
329	                f"mapping loads {mapping.entity_id}. An edge is declared by the entity it "
330	                f"runs from, because that is the row the target expression reads."
331	            )
332	        tables = {table.table for table in mapping.tables}
333	        if edge.source_table not in tables:
334	            raise MappingError(
335	                f"{where}: M6 -- {edge_id} names source_table {edge.source_table!r}, which is "
336	                f"not byte-identical to any table in its group ({sorted(tables)}). The engine "
337	                f"skips a relationship whose source_table it cannot match, in silence, and "
338	                f"the inherited key is then null on every row."
339	            )
340	        target = next((one for one in mappings if one.entity_id == declared.target_entity_id), None)
341	        if target is None:
342	            raise MappingError(
343	                f"{where}: M6 -- {edge_id} points at {declared.target_entity_id}, which no "
344	                f"mapping loads. There is nothing for the pairs to join to."
345	            )
346	        keys = {key_shape(key) for table in target.tables for key in table.primary_keys}
347	        if key_shape(edge.target_expression) not in keys:
348	            raise MappingError(
349	                f"{where}: M6 -- {edge_id} targets {edge.target_expression!r}, which is not "
350	                f"shaped like {declared.target_entity_id}'s own key ({sorted(keys)} with the "
351	                f"names taken out). The column may be named anything; the casting may not "
352	                f"differ, because a bare column and a cast produce different keys and the "
353	                f"pairs then join to nothing."
